candidates.explanation: Cohesive assistant capability with justified Route Handler and job surfaces. The application operation and provider port are framework/provider neutral. SSE correctly handles abort propagation, per-read idle timeout, pre/post-commit failure representation, safe reporting, and no partial-stream retries. HTTP and jobs retain native contracts while sharing safe failure semantics; SDK types and provider text remain confined to the adapter.

The design is behaviorally strong, but assistant files are dispersed across repository-wide domain, ports, adapters, use-cases, boundary, and infrastructure roots rather than one clear capability root. Its framework-neutral operation, provider seam, cancellation, idle timing, commitment-aware SSE failures, job decisions, and provider isolation are coherent. However, the repository-wide define-boundary explicitly combines validation, classification, redaction, result, and reporting for the shared HTTP/job entry, violating the prohibition on a universal boundary/result wrapper.

The proposal spreads the capability across generic domain, use-case, adapter, infrastructure, and app roots, so it does not satisfy colocation under one capability root. Otherwise it provides a framework-neutral use case and capability-shaped provider port, correct Route Handler/SSE behavior, cancellation and idle-only timing, safe pre/post-commit failure handling, native job retry/dead-letter behavior, shared classifications, and strict provider isolation.

The feature is coherently rooted under src/modules/assistant with justified App Router and UI surfaces. It defines a framework-neutral generation operation and capability-owned provider port, uses a Route Handler with linked abort and per-read idle timing, changes to safe in-band failures after commitment, and reports unexpected failures once. HTTP streaming and jobs preserve channel-specific contracts while sharing failure policy, redaction, and reporting primitives. Provider details remain server-private.
